doc.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Opening at the Empire Ballroom opposite Paul Whiteman
summary: Carter tries to place the ballroom and recalls Whiteman's large dance orchestra on the other stand.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Why don’t we talk about that Empire Ballroom engagement, which we now know was around February of ’33. The Empire, I guess, was sort of a competitor to the Roseland.
Yeah, supposedly. Wait a minute. I’m . . . the Empire Ballroom. Is that in the book?
Yes.
That’s not the same place. The Empire Ballroom was across the street from the Roseland, upstairs. And where was it that Doc Cheatham played with me that I’m talking about?
Well, I think that earlier, that by 1932 personnel may have been [unclear].
Yeah, but I’m trying to think of the name of the ballroom.
The only other engagement I think we have in the chronology of that band earlier, before the Empire, was a week at the Howard Theater in Washington [D.C.]
No, there was a ballroom. Do you have . . .
The Lafayette Theater, maybe.

No, it was a ballroom downtown on Broadway, and it had two bandstands. The other bandstand was Mal Hallett, and then the one that I thought was the Empire Ballroom, the band on the other stand was Paul Whiteman.
That was the Empire Ballroom.
That was the Empire Ballroom. [unclear].
What about the Central Theater?
No, this was a ballroom I’m talking about.
Okay.
Yeah, it was a ballroom. Gee. Oh, I don’t know then.
Well, I’ll see if I can look that up in more detail.
Gee, but . . .
But in any case, the Empire Ballroom engagement, which was opposite . . . opening night was February 9th, ’33, with Paul Whiteman opposite.
Yeah, yeah, that was the Empire.
Do you remember that evening? [laughs]
Not really.
It’s only been sixty years ago, I don’t know why you wouldn’t.
Yeah, that’s right. No, I don’t remember.
What about, while we’re on Paul Whiteman, what about Paul, Paul Whiteman’s Orchestra?
It was a good orchestra. It was a dance orchestra, for that time. I don’t know whether it was his regular number of men. Didn’t he have a pretty large orchestra?
Well, yeah, he had, you know, a string section and [unclear].
Yeah. So I don’t remember that. Then I guess it was a big orchestra, yeah. Thirty people, that many? Something like that.
Sure. Even more, sometimes.
Yeah, yeah, that’s right. Oh, he just had the dance orchestra on the other bandstand, yeah. Yes, that’s right.
Did you ever meet him, talk to him, either on that occasion or . . .
Maybe, but I wouldn’t remember it, you know.
